AGRICULTURE — MOCK EXAM #7
====

GRADE: Grade 4
SUBJECT: AGRICULTURE
TIME ALLOWED: 90 minutes
TOTAL MARKS: 80
ASSESSMENT: CBC school-based practice paper

INSTRUCTIONS
----
1. Answer all questions.
2. For calculations, show your working and write the units.
3. For multiple choice, choose the one best answer.
4. Check your work before you hand in.

SECTION A — MULTIPLE CHOICE
----
1. What is the purpose of sticks at the bottom of the compost heap? (1 mark)
   A. They make it look neat
   B. They let air move through the heap
   C. They add plant food
   D. They keep the heap dry forever

2. Which waste should NOT be put in a compost heap? (1 mark)
   A. Banana peelings
   B. Fresh grass
   C. Chicken droppings
   D. Plastic bags

3. Which sign shows that compost is ready? (1 mark)
   A. It is grey and hard
   B. It is hot and full of whole peelings
   C. It is wet and smells sour
   D. It is dark, crumbly and smells like fresh earth

4. Why does a higher container give a faster drip? (1 mark)
   A. It has a lid
   B. It has more air
   C. It is nearer the sun
   D. Gravity pushes the water more strongly

5. How can you tell that a plant has enough water? (1 mark)
   A. The leaves are gone
   B. The soil is damp about a finger deep
   C. The pot is empty
   D. The soil is dust

6. What should you do if a hole in a drip pipe is blocked? (1 mark)
   A. Clear it gently with a thin wire
   B. Pour hot oil in it
   C. Throw away the whole system
   D. Cut the pipe in half

7. Why is wet firewood a poor fuel? (1 mark)
   A. It makes a lot of smoke and gives little heat
   B. It burns very hot
   C. It has no smoke
   D. It lasts forever

8. How can a family get firewood without destroying forests? (1 mark)
   A. Cut young trees only
   B. Plant trees on their own land and replace those cut
   C. Burn grass
   D. Cut trees from forests at night

9. Why should food be cut into small pieces before cooking? (1 mark)
   A. They need more water
   B. They burn the pot
   C. They take longer to cook
   D. Small pieces cook faster and use less fuel

10. Why does a scarecrow need a hat and clothes? (1 mark)
   A. To keep warm
   B. To dry the crops
   C. To store food
   D. To look like a person and frighten animals

11. How fine should the soil in the seedbed be? (1 mark)
   A. Full of big clods
   B. Crumbly like brown sugar
   C. Hard like stone
   D. Wet like mud

12. Why is it best to plant fruit varieties that suit the local climate? (1 mark)
   A. They cost more
   B. They need no water
   C. They never get pests
   D. They grow and fruit better

13. Which of these is a climbing fruit? (1 mark)
   A. Mango
   B. Grapes
   C. Orange
   D. Guava

14. Which sign shows that a guava is ripe? (1 mark)
   A. It turns yellowish and smells sweet
   B. It has flowers on it
   C. It is dry and black
   D. It is dark green and hard

15. What is the main job of the trunk of a tree? (1 mark)
   A. Absorb sunlight
   B. Collect rain
   C. Carry water and food between roots and leaves
   D. Make flowers

16. How does eating fruit help our health? (1 mark)
   A. It makes us weak
   B. It gives only sugar and nothing else
   C. It gives vitamins and fibre
   D. It stops us drinking water

17. Which of these is an indigenous chicken called in Kenya? (1 mark)
   A. Kienyeji
   B. Turkey
   C. Broiler
   D. Layer only

18. What is the meat of sheep called? (1 mark)
   A. Beef
   B. Mutton
   C. Pork
   D. Bacon

19. Which drink is best with meals? (1 mark)
   A. Only soda
   B. Dirty water
   C. Clean water
   D. Only sugary juice

20. Which is a cheap way of getting a balanced meal? (1 mark)
   A. Eat only sweets
   B. Grow vegetables and fruits at home
   C. Skip meals
   D. Buy only expensive foods

21. What is the first thing to do with leftover cooked food? (1 mark)
   A. Leave it on the floor
   B. Leave it in the sun
   C. Cover it and store it safely
   D. Throw it in the road

22. Which food is usually boiled? (1 mark)
   A. Bhajia
   B. Potatoes
   C. Mandazi
   D. Chips

23. What should you hold hot pots with? (1 mark)
   A. A dry cloth or oven gloves
   B. Bare hands
   C. Paper
   D. A wet cloth

24. When should you wash your hands? (1 mark)
   A. Before eating and after using the toilet
   B. Only after school ends
   C. Never
   D. Only on Sunday

25. Why should a rubbish bin have a lid? (1 mark)
   A. To keep out flies and rats
   B. To make it heavy
   C. To look pretty
   D. To stop rubbish from rotting

26. What should you do after mopping a floor? (1 mark)
   A. Run on it
   B. Put up a sign that the floor is wet
   C. Pour more water
   D. Sweep it

27. What is the first step in cleaning gumboots? (1 mark)
   A. Put them in the fire
   B. Dry them in strong sun
   C. Store them wet
   D. Knock off lumps of mud outside

28. Why should PPE be cleaned? (1 mark)
   A. To make it smell
   B. Dirty PPE lasts longer
   C. Clean PPE is heavier
   D. Dirty PPE can carry germs

29. Which kind of PPE is suitable for handling compost? (1 mark)
   A. A necktie
   B. Shorts only
   C. Gloves and gumboots
   D. A dress only

30. Which item can be made with tacking stitches in this lesson? (1 mark)
   A. A roof
   B. A car
   C. A house
   D. A handkerchief

SECTION B — STRUCTURED / SHORT ANSWERS
----
31. A family boils beans for a long time on a big fire with the lid off. Suggest five ways to improve fuel use. (5 marks)

32. Plan a weekly cleaning schedule for the classroom using dusting, sweeping, mopping and refuse disposal. (5 marks)

33. List three safety rules when harvesting fruit. (3 marks)

34. Give two disadvantages of shallow frying. (2 marks)

35. Describe how to make a bottle drip for one plant. (3 marks)

36. State three dangers of using fuels at home and how to avoid one of them. (3 marks)

37. Explain why tacking thread should be loose. (2 marks)

38. Explain the difference between variety and proportion in a meal. (3 marks)

39. Name two woody fruit trees and two climbing fruit crops. (4 marks)

40. Explain how animals help crops grow. (3 marks)

41. Name two things that should never be put in a compost heap and say why. (2 marks)

42. Choose PPE for gardening and say why. (3 marks)

43. Explain the meaning of personal hygiene. (2 marks)

44. Give three times when you should wash your hands. (3 marks)

45. Why should an adult make the holes in the pipe? (2 marks)

46. Explain how measuring skills help you in tacking. (3 marks)

47. Name two problems that can attack ripe fruits. (2 marks)
pages.answers:
AGRICULTURE — MOCK EXAM #7 · MARKING SCHEME
====

SECTION A
----
1. B — They let air move through the heap
   Air helps the tiny living things rot the wastes.

2. D — Plastic bags
   Plastic does not rot and spoils the compost.

3. D — It is dark, crumbly and smells like fresh earth
   Ready compost looks and smells like soil and the materials cannot be recognised.

4. D — Gravity pushes the water more strongly
   A higher container gives a bigger push for water flowing down.

5. B — The soil is damp about a finger deep
   Feeling the soil shows if the roots have water.

6. A — Clear it gently with a thin wire
   A thin wire clears blockages without damaging the pipe.

7. A — It makes a lot of smoke and gives little heat
   Wet wood wastes heat drying itself.

8. B — Plant trees on their own land and replace those cut
   Growing trees keeps a supply of wood.

9. D — Small pieces cook faster and use less fuel
   Small pieces heat through quickly.

10. D — To look like a person and frighten animals
   Animals fear people, so a figure like a person scares them.

11. B — Crumbly like brown sugar
   Fine crumbly soil lets seeds come up easily.

12. D — They grow and fruit better
   Wrong climate gives poor growth.

13. B — Grapes
   Grapes grow on vines.

14. A — It turns yellowish and smells sweet
   Ripe guavas change colour and smell sweet.

15. C — Carry water and food between roots and leaves
   The trunk is like a pipe for the plant.

16. C — It gives vitamins and fibre
   Fruits protect the body and help digestion.

17. A — Kienyeji
   Kienyeji chickens are local breeds.

18. B — Mutton
   Mutton is sheep meat.

19. C — Clean water
   Water is essential and healthy.

20. B — Grow vegetables and fruits at home
   A kitchen garden gives fresh food.

21. C — Cover it and store it safely
   Covered food stays safe from flies.

22. B — Potatoes
   Potatoes are commonly boiled.

23. A — A dry cloth or oven gloves
   Wet cloth lets heat through.

24. A — Before eating and after using the toilet
   These are key times.

25. A — To keep out flies and rats
   Lids stop pests.

26. B — Put up a sign that the floor is wet
   Wet floors are slippery.

27. D — Knock off lumps of mud outside
   This removes the dirt before washing.

28. D — Dirty PPE can carry germs
   Clean PPE is safe and lasts longer.

29. C — Gloves and gumboots
   They protect hands and feet.

30. D — A handkerchief
   A handkerchief is an easy first item.

SECTION B
----
31. (5 marks)
   Answer: Soak the beans first, cook with the lid on, use dry wood, reduce the flame after boiling starts, cut food or use an improved jiko, put out the fire after cooking.
   Working / marking points: 1 mark for each correct way.

32. (5 marks)
   Answer: A table of days with jobs for each learner group: Monday dusting, Tuesday sweeping, Wednesday mopping, and refuse disposal each day, with tools and safety measures.
   Working / marking points: 2 marks for jobs, 1 for tools, 1 for safety, 1 for fairness of sharing.

33. (3 marks)
   Answer: Use a ladder or picking pole; do not climb thin branches; wash hands and fruit; use both hands (any three).
   Working / marking points: 1 mark for each rule.

34. (2 marks)
   Answer: It can splash and burn, and too much oil is not good for health.
   Working / marking points: 1 mark for each disadvantage.

35. (3 marks)
   Answer: Make tiny holes in the cap, fill the bottle with clean water, bury the neck upside down near the plant, press soil around it and refill when empty.
   Working / marking points: 1 mark for holes in cap, 1 mark for placing near plant, 1 mark for filling and refilling.

36. (3 marks)
   Answer: Fire burns, charcoal fumes are poisonous and gas can leak. Avoid one by keeping children away from fire, cooking in a place with fresh air or closing the gas valve after use.
   Working / marking points: 2 marks for dangers, 1 mark for a correct way to avoid one.

37. (2 marks)
   Answer: Tight thread pulls and wrinkles the cloth.
   Working / marking points: 1 mark for pulls, 1 mark for wrinkles.

38. (3 marks)
   Answer: Variety is eating many kinds of food; proportion is eating the right amount of each kind.
   Working / marking points: 1 mark for variety, 1 mark for proportion, 1 mark for an example.

39. (4 marks)
   Answer: Woody: guava, tree tomato, mango; climbing: passion fruit, grapes, kiwi, blackberry.
   Working / marking points: 1 mark for each correct example.

40. (3 marks)
   Answer: Their dung is used as manure, which feeds the soil, and oxen can be used to plough. Crops then grow well.
   Working / marking points: 1 mark for manure, 1 for ploughing, 1 for better crops.

41. (2 marks)
   Answer: Plastic and glass, because they do not rot.
   Working / marking points: 1 mark for two items, 1 mark for the reason.

42. (3 marks)
   Answer: Gloves protect hands from dirt and cuts; gumboots protect feet from mud; hat protects the head from the sun.
   Working / marking points: 1 mark for each item with reason.

43. (2 marks)
   Answer: Keeping our own body clean to stay healthy.
   Working / marking points: 1 mark for keeping clean, 1 mark for health.

44. (3 marks)
   Answer: Before eating, after using the toilet, after playing outside, after touching animals, after coughing (any three).
   Working / marking points: 1 mark for each.

45. (2 marks)
   Answer: Nails and awls are sharp and can hurt children.
   Working / marking points: 1 mark for sharp tools, 1 mark for safety or injuries.

46. (3 marks)
   Answer: Measuring gives correct stitch lengths, straight lines and correct size of the item.
   Working / marking points: 1 mark for each.

47. (2 marks)
   Answer: Fruit flies, birds or monkeys (any two).
   Working / marking points: 1 mark for each.
